step1_figure.circuit_type: Two-stage operational amplifier with indirect feedback compensation
step1_figure.description: The netlist implements a two-stage CMOS op-amp. It uses a common-gate MOSFET (MCG) to indirectly feed back the compensation capacitor current to the output of the first stage, which eliminates the right-half-plane (RHP) zero and improves stability and speed.

unity_gain_frequency.description: The frequency at which the open-loop voltage gain drops to 0 dB (1 V/V).

equation.explanation: Determines the bandwidth of the op-amp, set by the input pair transconductance and the compensation capacitor.
equation.assumptions: Assumes the second pole is at a much higher frequency than f_un.

sky130_expected.calculation: Assuming I_tail = 20uA -> I_D1 = 10uA. With V_GS - V_th ≈ 0.1V, g_m1 = 2*I_D1/(V_GS-V_th) = 200uA/V. f_un = 200uA/V / (2 * pi * 240fF) ≈ 132 MHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Depends heavily on the exact W/L sizing of the input pair which sets g_m1, but the 240fF capacitor targets ~100-150 MHz bandwidth.

open_loop_gain.description: The DC voltage gain of the op-amp without any feedback.

equation.explanation: The product of the intrinsic gains of the first (differential) and second (common-source) stages.

sky130_expected.calculation: R_1 = r_o1 || r_o3 ≈ 500kΩ. A_1 = g_m1 * R_1 = 200uA/V * 500kΩ = 100 V/V. Assuming second stage has similar gain A_2 ≈ 100 V/V. A_OL = 100 * 100 = 10000 V/V = 80 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Typical two-stage op-amps in 130nm achieve 60-80 dB depending on channel lengths and cascoding.

lhp_zero.description: Left-half-plane zero introduced by the indirect compensation scheme.

equation.explanation: The common-gate transistor MCG creates a zero in the left half plane, which adds positive phase shift and improves phase margin.
equation.assumptions: Assumes the resistance looking into MCG source is 1/g_mcg.

sky130_expected.calculation: Assuming g_mcg is sized similarly to g_m1 (≈ 200uA/V), f_z = 200uA/V / (2 * pi * 240fF) ≈ 132 MHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Designed to be near or slightly above the unity-gain frequency to boost phase margin.

second_pole.description: The second dominant pole of the op-amp, which degrades phase margin.

equation.explanation: The location of the second pole is pushed to a higher frequency compared to standard Miller compensation, allowing for higher bandwidth.

sky130_expected.calculation: With indirect compensation, f_2 is pushed significantly higher than f_un. Expected to be > 2 * f_un to maintain >60 deg phase margin.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Indirect compensation splits the poles more effectively, moving f_2 to a higher frequency.

slew_rate.description: The maximum rate of change of the output voltage during large-signal transients.

equation.explanation: Limited by the tail current of the differential pair charging/discharging the compensation capacitor.
equation.assumptions: Assumes the second stage can sink/source enough current to not be the bottleneck.

sky130_expected.calculation: Assuming I_tail = 20uA and C_c = 240fF. SR = 20uA / 240fF = 83.3 V/us.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The small 240fF compensation capacitor allows for a very high slew rate compared to standard Miller compensation.

equation.explanation: Ratio of differential gain to common-mode gain.

sky130_expected.calculation: Determined by the output resistance of the tail current source. A_c ≈ - (R_1 / (2 * R_tail)). With cascode tail, R_tail is very high, yielding CMRR > 60dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The use of cascode current sources in the tail significantly improves CMRR.

equation.explanation: Measures how well the amplifier rejects noise from the positive supply rail.

sky130_expected.calculation: Indirect compensation improves PSRR+ because the compensation capacitor is not tied directly to the VDD-referenced PMOS load.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Typically tracks the open-loop gain at DC.

step3_testbench.description: Measures Open-Loop Gain, Unity-Gain Frequency, Phase Margin, Slew Rate, and PSRR+ using a single testbench with ngspice alter commands.
